blocks.heading: CMU AI Research Commercialization
paragraphs: Carnegie Mellon University's School of Computer Science — the world's most commercially productive CS school — produces AI research that is commercializing in Pittsburgh and globally. ClickMasters productionizes CMU research:

Natural language processing: CMU's Language Technologies Institute produces NLP research that is among the most cited in the world — ClickMasters builds production NLP systems grounded in LTI research for Pittsburgh's technology companies.
Computer vision and robotics: CMU's Robotics Institute and the groundbreaking AV perception research produced at CMU create commercial CV opportunities for Pittsburgh's large AV technology community.
Human-computer interaction: CMU's HCII (Human-Computer Interaction Institute) produces AI/UX research that creates product development opportunities for Pittsburgh's technology product companies.

blocks.heading: Healthcare (UPMC)
paragraphs: UPMC (Pittsburgh HQ) is the US's largest integrated physician practice — 40 hospitals, 700 medical and nursing facilities, and 90,000+ employees:
HIPAA-compliant clinical AI for UPMC's Epic-integrated network.
Cancer research AI for UPMC Hillman Cancer Center (one of 71 NCI-designated comprehensive cancer centers).
Population health analytics for UPMC's large Pennsylvania Medicaid managed care program (UPMC for You).
Cost: $55,000–$155,000 | Timeline: 12–24 weeks | HIPAA, Pennsylvania Medicaid

blocks.heading: Autonomous Vehicle Technology
paragraphs: Aurora Innovation (Pittsburgh HQ), Waabi (Toronto HQ, Pittsburgh operations), and the AV technology companies that CMU's talent pipeline has attracted:
AV perception and planning AI: Computer vision, sensor fusion, and motion planning components for Pittsburgh's large AV technology community.
AV simulation: AI for synthetic data generation and simulation scenarios for AV safety validation.
Cost: $65,000–$175,000 | Timeline: 14–26 weeks | Safety-critical design

blocks.heading: Advanced Manufacturing and Materials

sections.title: Pittsburgh's AI Renaissance
sections.description: Pittsburgh's technology transformation from steel to AI is one of the US's great industrial city reinventions.

blocks.heading: Pittsburgh's AV technology concentration
paragraphs: The city that was home to US Steel's industrial might now hosts Aurora Innovation, Waabi, and the alumni companies of Argo AI (acquired by VW) — all companies that chose Pittsburgh specifically because of CMU's talent pipeline and Pittsburgh's unique combination of urban density (useful for AV data collection) and lower cost of living (competitive with Silicon Valley for non-equity compensation).

blocks.heading: CMU's commercial output
paragraphs: Carnegie Mellon's Computer Science School has produced founders and technical leaders at Google, Amazon, Apple, Meta, and dozens of AI companies — but increasingly, some of the most valuable commercialization is happening in Pittsburgh itself, where CMU's partnership with healthcare (UPMC has invested hundreds of millions in AI research) and manufacturing (numerous CMU-NIST manufacturing AI programs) creates commercial AI in Pittsburgh.

blocks.heading: UPMC's innovation programs
paragraphs: UPMC Enterprises — UPMC's commercialization and venture arm — has invested in dozens of healthcare AI companies and commercialized research from the University of Pittsburgh. UPMC's size (the 12th-largest employer in the US) creates an internal AI deployment market that would be the envy of many cities.
